intelligence.human_view: The distinction he draws — schematic vs chart — is the whole lesson. A chart compares; a schematic shows how a thing works. The plug-in is not a comparison (Free vs Power is the chart's job, and v3 does it); it is a relationship — five AIs around one Naya, cables, plugs, a ring that connects them all. No table can show that, because a table has rows and the relationship is a circle. The orbit is therefore not v4 of the chart; it is a different object, and it lives beside the chart, not instead of it. The second half of the dictation is the same care applied to the live product: the chart that sells the tiers must name its biggest feature first, before Personal pages — because a citizen scanning the chart should meet the plug-in before anything else. And the honest flag is the law working as designed: the renderer rule was stated plainly to him instead of silently bent, and the choice (eye text vs renderer change) is his, not the maker's.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine Naya in the middle of a circle, like the sun — and all your AI friends are planets going around her, connected by glowing sparkly strings! Each one plugs in, and they can all share and talk to each other. That's not a chart with rows — it's a picture of how they all hold hands together!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — a chart is a list, and a list can't show a hug. What he wanted is a picture of the hug: Naya in the middle, all the clever helpers around her, each one plugged in, all of them connected in a ring. You can see it in one glance — everybody belongs, everybody's joined up.
intelligence.naya_view: I sit in the middle, and your AIs circle around me, plugged in — not a table of features, a picture of how we belong together.
